chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Talking with fans and tiring in the interview
summary: Young people do not talk to him; Nat Hentoff will interview him next; illness limits his answers.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: What do they say when they talk to you?
HEMLOCK ERASABLE PAPER CONTENT
Who, the kids?
Yeah.
They don't talk to me.
They don't talk to you? Don't they ever come up and say, Mr. Mingus, --
Somebody will ask for autographs, about all. And I don't get talked to that easy.
No, it's true, you don't.
It's pretty hard to get this done.
I know it. I don't envy Nat, he's going to have his -- well, maybe Nat will come at it from a whole other angle. [NAT HENTOFF]
Well, it's like Mel Lewis. If the guy wouldn't ask the questions, and he wouldn't have nothing to say.
That's right, nothing the matter with that at all. People know what they got to say and then say it and don't say anything else, I got to respect that.
Yeah.
They may not get on the Johnny Carson Show again, but that's the price you have to pay for --.
Nat will probably have a bunch of questions already written out.
He probably does.
You had some when we started.
Yeah, I've gone through most of them.
And some of them, we lasted about 30 seconds on.
It's just very hard, being as sick as I am, to -- be ill, to comment long statements. I've got to get my breath to talk. I say short statements.
